headline: Most optimistic reporting season outcomes in large-to-midcap tech, with 50% of companies receiving EPS upgrades, as pessimism was more than priced in relative to business fundamentals
reasoning: Despite significant share price volatility during August driven by the so-called 'SaaS apocalypse' in calendar 2026, the technology sector was the only space in the ASX 200 where 50% of companies received EPS upgrades. Pretty attributes this to excessive pessimism already being baked into prices relative to underlying business fundamentals. This contrasts sharply with the materials, mining and energy sectors, which averaged an 8.4% cut to EPS estimates over the same period.
quote: The interesting thing for us was the IT space. So that's obviously been for the SAS apocalypse in calendar year 2026. The stock prices have been volatile and they were the most volatile part of the market in the month of August, the reporting season. But they also in amongst the large to midcaps. They seem to be the sector where the most optimistic outcomes came through, probably because there was more pessimism baked in than was warranted by the business fundamentals. So the industrial space, pardon me, the technology space was the only space where we saw 50% of companies actually get upgrades at the EPS line.
episode_title: Why selective industrials could offer the sweet spot

headline: ASX 200 reporting season delivered ~1% average revenue cuts, with ~2/3 of companies downgraded; cost pressures evident across market commentary and analyst numbers
reasoning: Martin Pretty notes that across the ASX 200, consensus estimates averaged a 1% cut at the revenue line, with roughly two-thirds of companies receiving downward revisions. Cost pressures are visible both in company commentary and analyst forecasts, manifesting as EBITDA compression without revenue relief — effectively the reverse of operating leverage. This is prompting companies to pursue cost-cutting strategies, with AI flagged as a tool for those who can deploy it effectively to reduce fixed overheads.
quote: Look, overall, if we look at the top 200 stocks where they're well covered by analysts, we we like to focus on looking at what the revisions the analysts put out, the consensus upgrades and downgrades are as an indication of sentiment towards the results. Obviously for the market's forward looking. So the S&P I SX200 on our numbers averaged the 1% cut at the revenue line. Roughly 2/3 of companies had estimates downgraded.

headline: AI efficiency gains seen as a meaningful cost-structure lever for companies that can deploy it effectively, especially to reduce fixed overheads

quote: Some companies are already really well established in terms of the strategies they're putting forward to adjust the cost structure to deal with the inflation and we think AI can play a role in that for those companies who know how to use AI efficiently and effectively, which is not always obvious to every company. headline: Equitable Investments bullish on cybersecurity sector as AI shifts from perceived threat to major growth driver
reasoning: Martin Pretty notes cybersecurity stocks sold off sharply earlier in the year on fears that AI would undermine business models, but sentiment has dramatically reversed. The Global Cybersecurity ETF rose 10.7% in a single week and 53% over three months. The new thesis is that AI creates a dual imperative for cybersecurity: enterprises need to secure their own AI infrastructure, and they need protection from bad actors who can now launch sophisticated attacks using AI with no technical skill. The convergence of quantum computing and AI adds another layer to what Pretty describes as an arms race, reinforcing the structural need for specialist cybersecurity providers.
quote: Last week alone, we saw the Global Cybersecurity ETF, which represents all the big cybersecurity players in the US and globally, up 10.7% in a week. It's up 53% over the past three months to the end of last week. And last night, I think it was up another almost 3.5%. So there's been a massive turn in sentiment and it is all driven by AI. So originally everyone saw AI as a huge threat. Now they're turning around and seeing AI as the opportunity. It's a necessity to have cyber security. In a world of AI.
